blocked_cross_source_operations.reason: General-population ever-use respondents 18+ versus selected online culture respondents 14–29, including minors and distinct questionnaire.
Different age ranges and survey questions from the same commissioned study; no shared-person overlap data or item denominators.
Cross-platform annual self-report respondent income versus selected monetized monthly YouTube client RPM.
Selected channels with earnings cannot be scaled to the general U.S. adult population or attempted publisher cohort.
NPORS 2026 adult ever-use across January–June and American Trends Panel August 2026 adult news behavior have different selection panels, time windows and questions.

Demographic composition within 2025 regular YouTube news consumers and 2026 share of adults who get news on YouTube have reversed conditional denominators, different periods and unknown joint response frames.

disclosure_rules: Do not use the total survey n as an individual item denominator when the report does not provide item response n.
Do not apply Pew's full-sample ±1.8-point uncertainty to a subgroup or external survey.
Do not infer identifiable respondent age, sex, ethnicity, religion or political opinions from usernames or view histories.
Aggregates covering ages under 18 do not authorize tracing or profiling individual minors.
Selected monetized YouTube channel-months exclude zero earners and cannot estimate first-time creator income.
Three 2026 survey samples and AIR client data are not independent measurements of one population outcome.
AI, paid creator marketing, public platform views, or advertiser reach do not provide survey-based unique-person identities.
The 2025 Pew NPORS general adult ever-use sample (5,022) is separate from the 2025 Pew ATP daily-frequency sample (5,123), although both appear in a single published report.

The 2025 and 2026 NPORS education and residence point estimates are comparable as named-question descriptive adult-survey responses, but separate people and unknown subgroup errors do not support a statistically significant trend finding.
